material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Field Primer for Engineered Wood Siding

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for factory-primed and bare engineered wood. NOT alkali-resistant — engineered wood is wood-based (neutral pH), not cementitious. Field prime is MANDATORY per LP SmartSide warranty even over factory primer. Must be top-coated within 180 days of installation. Products must be LP SmartSide-approved.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer system for NC engineered wood siding. Factory-primed surface has low porosity — higher coverage than bare wood. Bare wood (cut edges, damaged areas) absorbs more primer. No tannin-blocking needed — zinc borate treatment and MDI resin suppress extractive bleed.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Engineered Wood (ExpertFinish)

products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
primer.notes: Required for LP SmartSide ExpertFinish factory-finished products damaged during construction. The oven-baked factory finish is a non-standard substrate for field paint adhesion — bonding primer provides mechanical grip on the cured factory topcoat. Light scuff sand entire surface before priming.

material_systems.notes: Factory-finished surfaces are smooth and non-porous — good coverage. Key concern is adhesion, not sealing. Common NC scenario where factory finish is compromised during construction activity, caulking, or handling damage.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Engineered Wood Siding

finish.notes: LP SmartSide-approved products required for warranty compliance. QT2 allows single finish coat on properly primed surfaces. QT3 requires 2 coats standard. Minimum 15-year paint manufacturer warranty. Different approved product list than James Hardie.

material_systems.notes: Standard exterior production system. Flat is typical for siding field. Satin for accent or higher visibility areas. Engineered wood surface after priming provides consistent, predictable coverage.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Finish for Engineered Wood Siding

finish.notes: LP SmartSide-approved premium products. Superior color retention, fade resistance, UV stability. Light sand between coats on visible areas. Raking light inspection before second coat. 25+ year paint manufacturer warranty.

material_systems.notes: Premium exterior system for QT4 engineered wood siding. Semi-gloss available at QT4 for high-visibility accent areas.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Factory-primed engineered wood surface is sealed — consistent primer absorption. Non-porous factory coating provides good coverage. Smooth surface baseline.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Bare engineered wood at cut edges and damaged areas. OSB-core face is more porous than factory-primed surface. Lower coverage due to absorption into wood fiber matrix.

assumptions: Coverage rates are for smooth surfaces. Apply surface_texture_modifier to material quantity for textured profiles.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for 50-70% transfer efficiency.
Factory-primed engineered wood is slightly less porous than factory-primed natural wood — marginally better coverage.

SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED.notes: Factory-finished (ExpertFinish) surface is smooth and non-porous. Bonding primer spreads well — adhesion is the concern, not absorption.

assumptions: ExpertFinish surfaces are factory-smooth with texture embossing — lower texture modifier than bare wood.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency.

lap.notes: Smooth lap siding on primed surface. Consistent, predictable coverage. Long horizontal runs with lap edge overlap.

panel.notes: Large flat panels. Slightly better coverage than lap due to fewer edges and transitions.

t1_11.notes: Deep vertical grooves require additional material. Back-rolling distributes paint into grooves but consumes more product. Net coverage lower than lap or panel due to groove geometry.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET siding area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SIDING_FIELD).
Two-coat system is standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single coat.
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss.
T1-11 coverage penalty is due to groove geometry — similar concept to fiber cement shingle edge penalty.

consumables.name: Engineered wood end-cut edge sealer (LP SmartSide Cut End Seal)
consumables.notes: LP SmartSide-specific end-cut sealer. Seals field-cut edges to prevent moisture intrusion into OSB core — prevents irreversible thickness swell (springback). MOST CRITICAL consumable for this spec. Must be applied to ALL field-cut edges before or immediately after installation. Different product than fiber cement edge sealer — designed for OSB edge, not cementitious edge.

consumables.name: Exterior flexible paintable caulk
consumables.notes: Polyurethane or siliconized acrylic for siding-to-trim joints ONLY. Do NOT caulk field butt joints — creates moisture trap behind joint per research RF-012. Applied at siding-to-corner board, siding-to-window casing, and siding-to-door casing joints.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-180 grit
consumables.notes: For adhesion sanding on factory-primed and factory-finished surfaces. Light scuff to create mechanical profile. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.notes: For intercoat sanding at QT4. Light scuff between finish coats for adhesion and leveling. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 517 (lap/panel/T1-11 siding)
consumables.notes: 515 or 517 fan pattern for all engineered wood siding profiles. Standard tip selection for exterior latex on siding. Wood-fiber substrate causes less tip wear than cementitious fiber cement.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter (black) for latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment. Change when flow rate drops.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller cover for back-rolling
consumables.notes: Required for spray_backroll application method. 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap for smooth-to-moderate texture. Used to distribute spray-applied coating into T1-11 grooves and textured profiles. KEY DIFFERENCE from fiber cement — fiber cement does NOT use back-rolling. Replace when nap becomes saturated or matted.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller frame for back-rolling
consumables.notes: Heavy-duty 18-inch roller frame paired with CON_ENSD_ROLLER_18IN covers. Reusable across project. Extension pole required for elevated work.

consumables.name: 3-inch angular sash brush (exterior grade)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 200 LF of detail work
consumables.notes: For cut-in at siding-to-trim junctions, end-cut sealer application, and touch-up. Polyester/nylon blend for latex exterior coatings.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting / landscape tarps
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum for landscape, hardscape, and HVAC unit protection. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects.

consumables.name: Painter's tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway and patio protection. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.notes: For dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Latex paint cleanup solution
consumables.notes: For cleaning spray equipment, rollers, and brushes at end of each work session. Water-based systems — warm water with small amount of solvent for stubborn residue.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: House perimeter where landscape is adjacent — measured in LF along foundation/siding line
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based. Lay tarps along the perimeter of the house where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base only. Spray/spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings to catch overspray.

ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray/spray_backroll overspray protection.

ext_hardscape_patio.notes: Protection level driven by proximity and application method. Full cover for spray/spray_backroll operations.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures on or adjacent to siding
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible.

ext_hvac_unit.description: HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding
ext_hvac_unit.notes: Full tarp cover during spray/spray_backroll operations. Do not block intake/exhaust if unit is running.

compatibility_rules.description: Standard acrylic primer for factory-primed and bare engineered wood
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer is correct for all non-factory-finished engineered wood surfaces. Engineered wood is NOT alkaline — no alkali-resistant primer needed (KEY DIFFERENCE from fiber cement).

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer required for factory-finished surfaces (ExpertFinish)
compatibility_rules.notes: Oven-baked factory finish requires bonding primer for adhesion. Standard acrylic primer lacks adhesion on cured factory coating. Light scuff sand entire surface before bonding primer.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer needed for field-primed surfaces
compatibility_rules.notes: Direct topcoat on field-primed surfaces. Skip prime module entirely.

compatibility_rules.description: LP SmartSide-approved finish products for warranty compliance
compatibility_rules.notes: LP SmartSide warranty requires approved paint products. Product list is DIFFERENT from James Hardie-approved list. SW Duration, SW Emerald, BM Aura, and BM Regal Select are approved. Verify LP-specific PDS compatibility for any substitution.

compatibility_rules.description: No power washing on engineered wood
compatibility_rules.notes: High-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on engineered wood siding. Damages factory primer, forces water into OSB core at joints and cut edges, can cause irreversible swelling. Low-pressure wash only (garden hose + soft brush).

compatibility_rules.description: Back-rolling mandatory for T1-11 and recommended for textured profiles
compatibility_rules.notes: T1-11 deep vertical grooves require roller to distribute spray-applied coating into groove geometry. Spray-only leaves dry spots in grooves. Back-rolling also recommended for cedarmill and roughsawn textures on any profile.

compatibility_rules.description: Do NOT caulk field butt joints on engineered wood siding
compatibility_rules.notes: Caulking butt joints creates a moisture trap behind the siding plane. Engineered wood relies on the joint gap for drainage and ventilation behind the weather plane. Caulk siding-to-trim joints ONLY.

risk_notes.topic: OSB core springback at unsealed cut edges
risk_notes.risk: Unsealed field-cut edges allow moisture intrusion into OSB core, causing irreversible thickness swell (springback) due to MDI resin bond failure. Dimensional change is permanent and cannot be repaired. Most critical failure mode for engineered wood siding.
risk_notes.mitigation: Seal ALL field-cut edges with LP SmartSide Cut End Seal (CON_ENSD_END_SEALER) before or immediately after installation. This is a non-negotiable step.

risk_notes.risk: Factory primer degrades if exposed beyond 180 days. Becomes chalky, loses adhesion. Common on delayed NC projects.
risk_notes.mitigation: Field-prime and paint within 180 days of installation. If exposure exceeds 180 days, assess adhesion with tape pull test. May require sanding and re-priming.

risk_notes.risk: Airless spray and spray_backroll overspray drifts 10-15 ft. Can damage plantings, stain concrete, coat vehicles.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full landscape/hardscape protection for spray and spray_backroll applications. Wind monitoring — stop spray if wind exceeds 10 mph.

risk_notes.risk: Field painting over factory-finished (ExpertFinish) engineered wood voids the factory finish warranty.
risk_notes.mitigation: Document customer authorization before field-painting factory-finished products. The factory finish warranty is replaced by the field paint system warranty.

risk_notes.topic: Moisture content at joints and cut ends
risk_notes.risk: Engineered wood retains moisture longer at joints and cut ends than fiber cement. OSB core is more moisture-retentive than cementitious substrates. Painting over elevated MC causes adhesion failure and blistering.
risk_notes.mitigation: Check moisture content before painting — must be < 15% MC. Allow extra drying time at joints and cut ends, especially after rain events. Moisture meter check at cut ends is mandatory.

material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on engineered wood siding: 50-70% transfer efficiency. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50 to account for overspray, misting, and pattern overlap. Spray_backroll has slightly better transfer efficiency (~60-75%) because back-rolling recovers overspray on the surface.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: Cedarmill texture: multiply material by 1.20x. Roughsawn texture: multiply by 1.30x. Applied on top of profile coverage rate. Same factors as fiber cement — texture geometry determines consumption, not substrate material.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard coat system: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single finish coat. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime coat.
material_quantity_notes.t1_11_profile_premium: T1-11 profile consumes 25-35% more material than lap siding due to deep vertical groove geometry and mandatory back-rolling.
material_quantity_notes.back_roll_material_recovery: Back-rolling after spray distributes coating into grooves and textured surfaces. Net material consumption is slightly higher than spray-only due to thicker film build in grooves, but actual material waste (drips, runs) is lower.

assumptions.note: Factory-primed engineered wood is comparable to factory-primed fiber cement in porosity. Coverage rate matches fiber cement sibling.

assumptions.source: Research RF-001 (OSB core porosity), calibrated against COV_SDNG_PRIMER SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD rates
assumptions.note: Bare OSB-core face is more porous than factory-primed surface but less porous than rough-sawn natural wood. Coverage slightly better than natural bare wood.

assumptions.value: Single finish coat acceptable at QT2 on primed surfaces
assumptions.note: QT2 economy tier allows single coat — reduced labor and material. LP warranty requires minimum 2 coats but QT2 accepts the trade-off.

assumptions.source: No direct doctrine — extrapolated from fiber cement shingle coverage (COV_FCSD_FINISH shingle: 225-325 SF/gal)
assumptions.note: T1-11 groove geometry is conceptually similar to shingle edge geometry for material consumption. Coverage penalty comes from groove depth, not surface texture. Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.value: 1 EA roller cover per 500 SF back-rolled
assumptions.source: Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine general roller guidelines, adapted for exterior back-rolling
assumptions.note: No specific doctrine for 18-inch back-roll roller consumption on engineered wood. Rate estimated from general exterior roller guidelines. Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.source: LP SmartSide installation guide, adapted for painting scope
assumptions.note: End sealer consumption depends on cut end area (deeper cuts consume more). 150 ends per QT is conservative estimate. Fiber cement sibling uses 200 ends per QT — engineered wood OSB core absorbs more sealer.
